guarantees.claim: endian_swap, digest_swap, key_swap continuously reflect cfg_reg.endian_swap.q, cfg_reg.digest_swap.q, cfg_reg.key_swap.q respectively.

hw2reg.cfg fields are driven by direct copies or casts: hmac_en from cfg_reg.hmac_en.q, sha_en from cfg_reg.sha_en.q, digest_size from cast digest_size, key_length from cast key_length, endian_swap/digest_swap/key_swap from their respective cfg_reg.q.
reg_hash_start is asserted only when reg2hw.cmd.hash_start.qe and .q are both high; reg_hash_stop, reg_hash_continue, reg_hash_process follow the same pattern with their respective command fields.
hw2reg.err_code.de is driven by err_valid; hw2reg.err_code.d is driven by err_code.

hash_start is asserted when reg_hash_start, sha_en, ~cfg_block, and ~invalid_config are all high; hash_continue when reg_hash_continue, sha_en, ~cfg_block, ~invalid_config; hash_process when reg_hash_process, sha_en, cfg_block, ~invalid_config.
hash_start_or_continue is the logical OR of hash_start and hash_continue.

assumptions.claim: The reg2hw.cmd.*.qe and .q inputs form a glitch-free, single-cycle command pulse when both are high simultaneously.
assumptions.risk: If these signals are not properly synchronized or contain glitches, the resulting reg_hash_* combinational outputs could produce spurious pulses, causing unintended hash operations or state machine corruption in the SHA core.

assumptions.claim: sha_en, cfg_block, and invalid_config must be stable during the entire assertion window of reg_hash_start/continue/process pulses.
assumptions.risk: If any of these control signals change while reg_hash_* is high, the resulting hash_start/hash_continue/hash_process combinational outputs could glitch or be truncated, leading to mis-synchronization with the SHA engine or partial commands.

assumptions.claim: err_valid is asserted only when err_code is stable, and does not stay high across err_code changes if software expects clean latching.
assumptions.risk: If err_valid remains high and err_code changes, the error register will be overwritten each cycle, potentially causing software to read a transient or inconsistent error code, or missing a prior error.

uncertain_points.claim: hash_process uses cfg_block=1 while hash_start/hash_continue use ~cfg_block. It is not locally enforced that these commands are mutually exclusive in time or that cfg_block is static during active commands. The sha core and software must ensure no simultaneous assertion.
uncertain_points.cond: when cfg_block transitions near a command edge
uncertain_points.risk: Simultaneous activation of both types of commands could cause internal state machine conflicts in the SHA core, leading to incorrect hash computation.

uncertain_points.claim: invalid_config gates all hash commands, but its generation logic is not part of this chunk. It must accurately reflect illegal configurations (e.g., digest_size, key_length) and be asserted promptly before commands are issued.
uncertain_points.cond: when a software configuration is illegal but invalid_config is still low
uncertain_points.risk: A hash operation could proceed with an invalid configuration, potentially compromising security guarantees such as using a weak digest size.

uncertain_points.claim: The err_code register is updated combinatorially via err_valid; there is no edge detection or acknowledge mechanism visible. It is unclear if err_valid is pulsed for one cycle or if err_code can change while err_valid remains high.
uncertain_points.cond: when err_valid is high and err_code changes or err_valid is not a single-cycle pulse
uncertain_points.risk: Software may read a stale or intermediate error value, complicating error handling.

uncertain_points.claim: digest_size and key_length are cast to enum types for readback. It is not guaranteed that they only take legal enum values when invalid_config is low; illegal values could be exposed to software via hw2reg.
uncertain_points.cond: when digest_size or key_length has an out-of-range value while invalid_config is deasserted
uncertain_points.risk: Software might misinterpret a readback value, leading to misconfiguration decisions, but no direct hardware fault.
